newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bogota bomb blast wrecks Communist Party newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Bogota bomb blast wrecks Communist Party newspaper.

text.p: A bomb exploded in downtown Bogota on Sunday partly destroying the headquarters of the Communist Party newspaper and shattering windows in nearby offices, police said.
The 26-pound (12 kg) bomb blast about 4 a.m. (0900 GMT) caused no deaths or injuries but damaged at least 15 buildings including the Labour Ministry, Bogota Telephone Company offices and a theatre.
Bogota police chief Gen. Teodoro Ocampo said investigators were hunting for clues to the identity of the bombers.

Communist Party deputy leader Carlos Arturo Lozano blamed the attack on right-wing paramilitary groups and criticised Colombia's security forces for failing to protect the party's members and its weekly newspaper, called Voz (Voice).

"The paramilitaries recently held a national summit and threatened actions like this. This is definitely their work. We're totally defenceless against the extermination campaign that is being waged against our party," Lozano said.
It was the third major bomb attack in Colombia in a week.

A woman died and 48 people were injured when a bomb exploded outside the home of a newspaper editor and former politician in the northwest city of Medellin on Monday. The next day four people were killed and scores injured when a bomb ripped through the headquarters of a cattle ranchers federation in Monteria, in northwest Cordoba province.
A small bomb made of dynamite exploded in the former offices of the Communist Youth on Thursday close to the site of Sunday's explosion but caused little damage.
